variants.title: Potentiometer: internal resistance of a Daniell cell
variants.unknown: the internal resistance r of the Daniell cell
variants.note: Zn | ZnSO4 || CuSO4 | Cu has an emf of 1.10 V. A laboratory pot cell has a fairly high internal resistance, of the order of ohms, because of the wide gap and the porous pot between the plates.

source.title: NCERT Chemistry Part I, Class XII, Unit 2 Electrochemistry (Daniell cell, 1.10 V)
source.note: Internal resistance: typical value for a laboratory Daniell pot cell, not a property of a named product.

variants.title: Potentiometer: internal resistance of a fresh dry cell (size D)
variants.unknown: the internal resistance r of the dry cell
variants.note: A fresh zinc-carbon (Leclanché dry) cell reads about 1.5-1.6 V on open circuit; a fresh D cell's internal resistance is well under an ohm.

source.title: Linden's Handbook of Batteries (Reddy), chapter on zinc-carbon (Leclanché) cells
source.note: Open-circuit voltage 1.5-1.75 V when fresh; internal resistance rises as the cell is used.

variants.title: Potentiometer: internal resistance of a used dry cell
variants.unknown: the internal resistance r of the used dry cell
variants.note: As a dry cell is used its emf falls slowly while its internal resistance rises many times: that is why an old cell cannot drive a torch bulb though a voltmeter still shows 1.3 V.

source.title: Linden's Handbook of Batteries (Reddy), chapter on zinc-carbon (Leclanché) cells
source.note: Values for a partly discharged cell are typical, not a property of a named product.

variants.title: Potentiometer: internal resistance of an alkaline cell (size AA)
variants.unknown: the internal resistance r of the alkaline cell
variants.note: A fresh alkaline AA cell has an open-circuit voltage near 1.6 V and a low internal resistance, which rises as it is used.

source.title: Energizer E91 (AA alkaline) product datasheet
source.note: Internal resistance of a fresh cell listed as 150-300 milliohm.

variants.title: Potentiometer: a Leclanché cell after heavy use (polarised)
variants.sample: Leclanché cell, polarised after heavy use
variants.unknown: the internal resistance r of the polarised Leclanché cell
variants.note: A Leclanché cell that has given a large current for some time polarises: hydrogen collects at the carbon faster than the depolariser removes it, so its emf falls and its internal resistance rises. It recovers on rest.

source.title: NCERT Physics Laboratory Manual, Class XII: potentiometer experiments
source.note: Values are typical for a polarised laboratory Leclanché cell, not a property of a named product.
